column3: A verifying forgery under the honest key gives a canonical collision in the verifier's log, a WOTS hit on the verifier's hypertree path (the verifier hashes the honest chain value at a step below the digit the honest key signs there), a FORS hit (the verifier hashes the honest FORS secret at an index no signed message selects), or ITSR coverage. The extended game H1' appends, after H1 ends, challenger draws of the honest WOTS keys on the forged digest's path, of the FORS leaves at its indices, and (extTail) of the complete honest FORS key of the forged digest and the complete honest XMSS tree at every layer of the forged path, all computed recursively from the honest seeds, with the digest recomputed adversary-side; H1's draws are a prefix of H1''s, its output and key are H1's, and on every tape on which H1 is won the four events hold on H1''s table. No probability is bounded here

column3: For any symbolic program: before the first disagreement step, entries past the initial ones resolve to distinct requests; hence the first disagreement step is an adversary step or a challenger step whose symbolic lookup appends a new entry, unless two initial entries collide (initColl). The anyDis tapes are therefore bounded counting only probes at such eligible steps that also satisfy any tape-independent predicate Φ holding at every step with no earlier disagreement, split by the width of the pinned handle: #anyDis·256^W ≤ R^N·B_lo·256^(W-wmin) + R^N·B_hi + #(wildColl ∨ initColl)·256^W, with B_hi ≤ S^2 always. column3: In the extended game H1', every pre-step state reached without an earlier disagreement satisfies InvS (coins at entries 0-2, adversary entries carry no handles, revealed handles exist and are unprotected, every challenger entry belongs to a DSM request family, DistK past the coins), and each step meets its obligation: a challenger request is a key derivation, a PRF request at an in-range address of kind 5 or 6, the randomizer, the signing request, or a structured thash request whose address literal is in range, whose key is the tweak-key entry and whose k-th input handle resolves to the k-th canonical child of its address; a reveal discloses only existing unprotected handles. Structured requests at one address are one request, and two handles resolving to one canonical node are one handle. The invariant is structural (dataflow), holds on every tape, and is the input from which the Φ of C56 is to be derived; B_lo for H1' is not yet bounded

A narrow-shaped request's skeleton is determined by any bytes it is compatible with. Every narrow pin counted by hidden_bound_split is an adversary step against a coin or a skeleton-determined challenger entry (at most four per adversary step) or a fresh challenger step against an adversary entry (at most one per adversary entry), so B_lo ≤ 5·AA. Hence #anyDis(H1')·2^256 ≤ R^N·5·AA·2^(256-8n) + R^N·S^2 + #(wildColl ∨ initColl)(H1')·2^256, and for SPX128f #won·2^256 ≤ #canon·2^256 + JA·R^N·2^128 + 2·R^N·5·AA·2^128 + 2·R^N·S^2 + 2·#(wildColl ∨ initColl)(H1')·2^256. column2: SPHINCS_SECURITY_CHARTER (collisions of independently sampled values in H1')
column3: The hidden-value bound holds with the wild-guess/collision event restricted to steps with no earlier disagreement (wildCollP). At such steps of H1' no guess is wild (every handle of every entry and request is an existing entry of width n or 32), and an unopened collision of two distinct challenger requests forces two distinct 32-byte key entries (tweak key, PRF key, PRF-msg key) to agree; an initial collision is two coins agreeing modulo 256^n. So wildCollP ∨ initColl is a tape collision, of probability at most 3/2^(8n) + N^2/2^256. For SPX128f: Pr[won] ≤ Pr[canonical collision on H1''s table] + (JA + 10·AA + 6)/2^128 + 2·(S^2 + N^2)/2^256. The step bound S, the adversary-step bound AA, the canonical-collision count and the ITSR budgets are not yet discharged; SPX256f needs a wide-class count
